Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Ahmad al-Mawardi informed us, saying: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sadah al-Karabisi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Muslim ibn Qutaybah narrated to us, from Sa'id, from 'Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surah Qaf, Allah will make the pangs and agonies of death easy for him" [84] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/233.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

**Qaf.** Ibn 'Abbas said: It is one of the names of Allah, the Exalted, by which He swears. Qatadah said: It is one of the names of the Qur'an. Al-Qurazi said: It is the opening of the names of Allah: Qadir (the Able), Qadir (the Capable), Qahir (the Subduer), Qadi (the Judge), and Qabid (the Restrainer). Al-Sha'bi said: It is the opening of the surah. Buraydah, 'Ikrimah, and al-Dahhak said: It is a mountain surrounding the earth, made of green emerald; the greenness of the sky comes from it, the two sides of the sky rest upon it, and what the people have of emerald is what falls from the mountain. This is a narration of Abu al-Hawra', from Ibn 'Abbas.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Dhu al-Qarnayn came to Mount Qaf and saw small mountains around it. He asked it: "What are you?" It said: "I am Qaf." He asked: "What are these mountains around you?" It said: "They are my veins. There is no city among the cities except that it has a vein from it. When Allah wishes to shake that land, He commands me, and I move that vein, and that land is shaken." Dhu al-Qarnayn said: "O Qaf, tell me something of the greatness of Allah." It said: "Indeed, the affair of our Lord is great; attributes fall short of Him, and imaginations come to an end before Him."

He said: "Tell me the least of what can be described of it." It said: "Behind me there is a land, a distance of five hundred years, in a width of five hundred years, of mountains of ice, which crush one another. Were it not for that ice, they would have burned from the heat of Hell."

He said: "Tell me more." It said: "Gabriel, peace be upon him, stands before Allah, the Exalted, and his limbs tremble. Allah creates from each tremor one hundred thousand angels. These angels stand in rows before Allah, the Exalted, with their heads bowed. When Allah permits them to speak, they say: 'There is no god but Allah.' This is His saying: ﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks, none shall speak except one whom the Most Gracious permits, and he speaks what is right﴾ [[Surah al-Naba': 38.]], meaning: there is no god but Allah."

Al-Farra' said: I heard someone say: (Qaf) means: what is to occur has been decreed. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: Its meaning is: stop at Our command and Our prohibition, and do not transgress them. It was also said: Its meaning is: Say, O Muhammad.

Ahmad ibn 'Asim al-Antaki said: It refers to the nearness of Allah, the Exalted, to His servants. Its explanation is His saying: ﴿And We are nearer to him than the jugular vein﴾ [[Surah Qaf: 16.]]. Ibn 'Ata' said: He swears by the strength of the heart of His beloved Muhammad (ﷺ), since he bore the address and it did not affect him, because of the elevation of his state.

**By the Glorious Qur'an.** Noble, honored by Allah, the Great, the All-Aware.

The scholars differed concerning the answer to this oath. The people of Kufa said: the answer is ﴿Nay, but they wonder﴾. Al-Akhfash said: its answer is omitted, and its meaning is: "Qaf. By the Glorious Qur'an, you shall surely be raised." Ibn Kaysan said: its answer is His saying: ﴿...what word he utters...﴾ [the verse]. It was also said: the answer is "We have known."

The answers to oaths are seven: (inna), the emphatic particle, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord is ever watchful﴾ [[Surah al-Fajr: 14.]]; (ma), the negation, as in: ﴿By the morning brightness, your Lord has not forsaken you﴾ [[Surah al-Duha: 1–3.]]; the lam with fatha, as in: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ [[Surah al-Hijr: 92.]]; (in), the light form, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By Allah, we were surely in...﴾ [[Surah al-Shu'ara': 97.]]; (la), as in: ﴿And they swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that Allah will not raise up one who dies﴾ [[Surah al-An'am: 109.]]; (qad), as in: ﴿By the sun and its brightness... he has succeeded who purifies it﴾ [[Surah al-Shams: 1–9.]]; and (bal), as in: ﴿Qaf. By the Glorious Qur'an. Nay, but they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves﴾, whose lineage, lineage, truthfulness, and trustworthiness they knew. ﴿So the disbelievers said: "This is a strange thing"﴾, something astonishing.

﴿When we have died and become dust? That is a far return.﴾ The resurrection is omitted, because the context indicates it. It is said: "I returned him, a return," and he returned, a returning. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if Allah returns you to a faction of them﴾ [[Surah al-Tawbah: 83.]].

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿We have known what the earth consumes of them﴾, meaning what the earth eats of their bones and bodies. It was also said: its meaning is: We have known what decays of them and what remains, because the coccyx is not consumed by the earth, as came in the hadith: "Every son of Adam decays, except the coccyx, from which he was created and from which he will be reassembled" [[85] [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/251 and Musnad Ahmad: 2/499.]]. The bodies of the prophets and martyrs also do not decay.

Al-Suddi said: And death says: We have known who among them will die and who will remain.

﴿And with Us is a Book preserved﴾, protected from the devils and from being effaced or scattered. It is the Preserved Tablet, in which all decreed things are written.

﴿Nay, they denied the truth [the Qur'an] when it came to them, so they are in a confused state.﴾ Abu Hamzah said: Ibn 'Abbas was asked about "marij," and he said: "It is the mixed-up thing. Have you not heard the poet's saying:

"She moved about and sought him within her, so he sprang up as if he were a supple, swaying branch."" [[Taj al-'Arus: 2/100.]]

Al-Walibi reported from him: "a disordered matter." Al-'Awfi reported from him: "a matter of error." Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: "confused." Qatadah said: In this verse, whoever the truth descends upon, his affair becomes confused for him, and his religion becomes obscure to him. Ibn Zayd said: "mixed up." It was also said: "corrupt." It was also said: "changed." All these sayings are close in meaning. The root of "marij" is agitation and restlessness. It is said: "the affair of the people became disordered (maraja)," "the religion became disordered," and "the ring became loose on my finger" (maraja) if it became loose from thinness. The poet said:

"The religion became disordered, so I prepared for it a sturdy, high-withered, well-fleshed (mount)." [[Lisan al-'Arab: 10/408; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/15. "Al-hariq": the withers; "al-kutad": the junction of the two shoulders.]]

In a hadith: "Their covenants and their hopes became disordered (marijat)."

﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We built it and adorned it, and it has no rifts?﴾ That is: cracks and openings; its singular is "fari." Ibn Zayd said: "al-furuj" are things that are scattered and separated from one another. Al-Kisa'i said: There is no disparity or difference in it.

﴿And the earth — We spread it out﴾, extended it over the water. ﴿And We cast in it firm mountains, and caused to grow in it of every beautiful pair, a lovely (plant)﴾, good and noble, by which one is delighted, meaning: gladdened.

﴿As an insight﴾, meaning: We made that an insight. Abu Hatim said: it is in the accusative as an infinitive. ﴿And a reminder for every servant who turns in repentance﴾, meaning: an insight or a reminder of its turning to Him, because whoever is able to create the heavens, the earth, and the plants is able to resurrect them. Among the infinitives similar to "tabsira" are "takmila" and "tafdila," and among the doubled-root nouns are "nakhla" and "ba'ra."

﴿And We sent down from the sky blessed water, and caused to grow by it gardens and grain of the harvest﴾, meaning wheat, barley, and all grains that are harvested, stored, and eaten. He attributed "grain" (habb) to "harvest" (hasid), and they are one thing, because the wording differs, as one says "the mosque of the congregation" and "the spring of the first," and "the sure truth" and "the jugular vein," and the like.

﴿And the tall palm trees﴾. Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, and Qatadah said: tall. 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Had said: its stalk, for its straightness in height. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: upright. Al-Hasan and al-Farra' said: laden, heavy with fruit. It is said of a ewe when she gives birth: "she has given birth (absaqat)." Its position is in the accusative as a circumstantial state, and it is detached (from the preceding).

Al-Hasan informed me, saying: 'Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd ibn Muhammad ibn Subh al-Kinani narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Yunus al-Nahshali narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn 'Ilaqah, from Qutbah ibn Malik, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) recite: "wa-al-nakhla basiqat" with the sad [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/7.]].

﴿For it are spathes (talh) of dates, and fruit, a cluster-of-thread, arranged in rows.﴾ "Talh" means dates and fruit; it is so named because it emerges (yatli'). "Nadid" means arranged, piled up, with one part placed upon another. Ibn al-Ajda' said: The palm trees of Paradise are arranged in rows from their roots to their branches, and their fruit is like the buckets and pails, and their rivers flow in a ditch (akhdud), meaning: trenches.

﴿As provision for the servants; and We gave life thereby to a dead land.﴾ That is, We made it provision for the servants.

Ibn Manjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Saqlab narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Khasib narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Jawadi narrated to me, saying: 'Atiq ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Qudamah, from Abu 'Abd Allah al-Aghar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When the rain came to them and the gutters flowed, the Prophet (ﷺ) would say: "There is no drought upon you this year" [[86] [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 1/258.]]. That is: barrenness.

﴿Thus is the Resurrection (khurudj) from the graves.﴾

﴿Before them the people of Noah denied, and the companions of the Rass, and Thamud, and 'Ad, and Pharaoh, and the brothers of Lut, and the companions of the Thicket, and the people of Tubba'.﴾ Tubba' was the king of Yemen; he was called Tubba' because of the multitude of his followers. He used to worship fire, then embraced Islam and called his people to Islam. They were of Himyar, and they denied him. His account and the account of his people is what 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us: Abu 'Ali Isma'il ibn Sa'dan informed me, saying: 'Ali ibn Ahmad informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Jarir narrated to us; and 'Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them from Ibn Jarir, who said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying:

Tubba' the last, who was As'ad Abu Karib ibn Malki Karib, when he came from the East, made his route through Medina. When he passed by it, he did not disturb its people, but left behind among them a son of his, who was killed by treachery. He came to it, intending to expel its people and uproot them, and to cut down its palm trees. This tribe of the Ansar gathered for him when they heard of his intention, and they resisted him. Their leader on that day was 'Amr ibn Zalm, a brother of Banu al-Najjar, one of Banu 'Amr. They went out to fight him. Tubba' had come upon them before that, and a man among them, from Banu 'Adi ibn al-Najjar, called Ahmar, killed a companion of Tubba's, having found him in a palm-cluster of his at Jaddah, and struck him with a palm trunk and killed him.

He said: "Verily the date belongs to the one who pollinated it." Then, when he killed him, he threw him into one of their well-known wells, called Dhat Tawman. This increased Tubba's rage against them. While Tubba' was in that state of fighting them, they fought him and he fought them. He said: The Ansar claim that they fought him by day and hosted him by night. This pleased him, and he said: "By Allah, these people of ours are noble." Then two rabbis of the rabbis of the Jews of Banu Qurayzah came to him, two learned and firm scholars; they were the sons of 'Amr, and they were the most knowledgeable people of their time. They came to Tubba' when they heard what he intended, of destroying the city and its people. They said to him: "O King, do not do this, for if you do what you intend, you will be prevented from it, and you will not be safe from swift punishment." He said to them: "Why is that?" They said: "It is the place of emigration of a Prophet who will emerge from this tribe of Quraysh at the end of time; it will be his home and his dwelling." So he desisted from what he intended against Medina, and he saw that they had knowledge, and what he heard from them pleased him. They invited him to their religion, so he should follow them in their religion. Tubba' said concerning that:

"What is wrong with your sleep, like the sleep of one with sore eyes, sleepless, as if you never stop staying awake?

In rage against two sons of a branch who alighted at Yathrib: woe to them for the punishment of a corrupting day!

We descended upon Yathrib, our breasts boiling with its agitations for slaughter, with a reaping...

By the oath of patience I swore, an oath of commitment, by your life, not one of gnashing of teeth:

That I would come to Yathrib, I would not leave its midst without a single palm cluster or a dry date remaining in Yathrib ever again.

Until there came to me from Qurayzah a learned man, with news, by your life, about the Jews, a blackened one.

He said: 'Desist from a protected town for a Prophet of Makkah from Quraysh, a guided one.'

So I pardoned them with a pardon that does not reproach, and I left them for the punishment of an everlasting day.

And I left them to Allah, hoping for His pardon on the day of reckoning from the blazing Hell.

And I left in it for them from our people a band of men of lineage and praiseworthy courage.

A band in whose wake victory will be, hoping thereby for the reward of the Lord of Muhammad."" [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/533, and he mentioned the rest of the verses.]]

Then when [......] [[An illegible word.]] Tubba' went to their religion, he honored them, and departed from Medina, and took them with him to Yemen. When he approached Yemen to enter it, Himyar prevented him from that and said: "Do not enter it upon us, for you have departed from our religion." He invited them to his religion and said: "It is a religion better than your religion."

They said: "Then judge between us by the fire." In Yemen there was a fire at the foot of a mountain called Nada (so in the manuscript), to which they would bring their disputes; it would judge between them, consuming the wrongdoer and not harming the wronged. When they said this to Tubba', he said: "You have been fair." So his people went out with their idols and what they drew near to in their religion, and the two rabbis went out with their scriptures around their necks, wearing them, until they sat before the fire at the place from which it emerges. The fire came out toward them, but when it approached Himyar, they turned away from it and feared it. Those present from the people called to them and urged them to be patient with it, and they were patient until it overwhelmed them, and it consumed the idols and what they had brought near, and some men of Himyar who carried them. The two rabbis came out with their scriptures around their necks, reciting the Torah, their foreheads sweating, and it did not harm them. The fire recoiled until it returned to its exit from which it had come. At that, Himyar embraced the religion of the two rabbis.

From there came the origin of Judaism in Yemen [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/200.]].

They had a house which they revered, sacrificing beside it and speaking from it while they were upon their polytheism. The two Qurayzah rabbis, whose names were Ka'b and Asad, said to Tubba': "It is nothing but a devil [who deludes them and plays with them], so leave us alone with it." He said: "Then it is your affair with it." They brought out from it a black dog and slaughtered it, then they demolished that house, and its remnants are in Yemen today, as has been mentioned to me.

Abu Dawud narrated from Abu Hatim, from al-Riyashi, who said: Abu Karib As'ad al-Himyari was one of the Tubba's. He believed in the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) seven hundred years before he was sent, and he composed a poem about that:

"I testify concerning Ahmad that he is a messenger from Allah, Creator of souls.

Were my life extended to his lifespan, I would be his in-law and his paternal cousin." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/145.]]

﴿Each one denied the messengers, so My warning was justly due.﴾ That is: the threat of punishment for them, warning the disbelievers of Makkah. Qatadah said: Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, destroyed the people of Tubba', and He did not destroy him. He was one of the kings of Yemen. He marched with armies, conquered lands, and headed for Makkah to demolish the House. It was said to him: "This House has a Lord who protects it." He repented, entered Makkah in the state of ihram, circumambulated the House, and clothed it. He was the first to clothe the House.

﴿Were We then wearied by the first creation?﴾ That is: were We incapable of it, and was the first creation beyond Our power? ﴿Nay, they are in confusion about a new creation﴾, which is the resurrection.

Al-Hasan informed me, saying: 'Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd ibn Muhammad ibn Subh al-Kinani narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Yunus al-Nahshali narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn 'Ilaqah, from Qutbah ibn Malik, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) recite: "wa-al-nakhla basiqat" with the sad [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/7.]].

﴿For it are spathes (talh) of dates, and fruit, a cluster-of-thread, arranged in rows.﴾ "Talh" means dates and fruit; it is so named because it emerges (yatli'). "Nadid" means arranged, piled up, with one part placed upon another. Ibn al-Ajda' said: The palm trees of Paradise are arranged in rows from their roots to their branches, and their fruit is like the buckets and pails, and their rivers flow in a ditch (akhdud), meaning: trenches.

﴿As provision for the servants; and We gave life thereby to a dead land.﴾ That is, We made it provision for the servants.

Ibn Manjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Saqlab narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Khasib narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Jawadi narrated to me, saying: 'Atiq ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Qudamah, from Abu 'Abd Allah al-Aghar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When the rain came to them and the gutters flowed, the Prophet (ﷺ) would say: "There is no drought upon you this year" [[86] [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 1/258.]]. That is: barrenness.

﴿Thus is the Resurrection (khurudj) from the graves.﴾

﴿Before them the people of Noah denied, and the companions of the Rass, and Thamud, and 'Ad, and Pharaoh, and the brothers of Lut, and the companions of the Thicket, and the people of Tubba'.﴾ Tubba' was the king of Yemen; he was called Tubba' because of the multitude of his followers. He used to worship fire, then embraced Islam and called his people to Islam. They were of Himyar, and they denied him. His account and the account of his people is what 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us: Abu 'Ali Isma'il ibn Sa'dan informed me, saying: 'Ali ibn Ahmad informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Jarir narrated to us; and 'Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them from Ibn Jarir, who said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying:

Tubba' the last, who was As'ad Abu Karib ibn Malki Karib, when he came from the East, made his route through Medina. When he passed by it, he did not disturb its people, but left behind among them a son of his, who was killed by treachery. He came to it, intending to expel its people and uproot them, and to cut down its palm trees. This tribe of the Ansar gathered for him when they heard of his intention, and they resisted him. Their leader on that day was 'Amr ibn Zalm, a brother of Banu al-Najjar, one of Banu 'Amr. They went out to fight him. Tubba' had come upon them before that, and a man among them, from Banu 'Adi ibn al-Najjar, called Ahmar, killed a companion of Tubba's, having found him in a palm-cluster of his at Jaddah, and struck him with a palm trunk and killed him.

He said: "Verily the date belongs to the one who pollinated it." Then, when he killed him, he threw him into one of their well-known wells, called Dhat Tawman. This increased Tubba's rage against them. While Tubba' was in that state of fighting them, they fought him and he fought them. He said: The Ansar claim that they fought him by day and hosted him by night. This pleased him, and he said: "By Allah, these people of ours are noble." Then two rabbis of the rabbis of the Jews of Banu Qurayzah came to him, two learned and firm scholars; they were the sons of 'Amr, and they were the most knowledgeable people of their time. They came to Tubba' when they heard what he intended, of destroying the city and its people. They said to him: "O King, do not do this, for if you do what you intend, you will be prevented from it, and you will not be safe from swift punishment." He said to them: "Why is that?" They said: "It is the place of emigration of a Prophet who will emerge from this tribe of Quraysh at the end of time; it will be his home and his dwelling." So he desisted from what he intended against Medina, and he saw that they had knowledge, and what he heard from them pleased him. They invited him to their religion, so he should follow them in their religion. Tubba' said concerning that:

"What is wrong with your sleep, like the sleep of one with sore eyes, sleepless, as if you never stop staying awake?

In rage against two sons of a branch who alighted at Yathrib: woe to them for the punishment of a corrupting day!

We descended upon Yathrib, our breasts boiling with its agitations for slaughter, with a reaping...

By the oath of patience I swore, an oath of commitment, by your life, not one of gnashing of teeth:

That I would come to Yathrib, I would not leave its midst without a single palm cluster or a dry date remaining in Yathrib ever again.

Until there came to me from Qurayzah a learned man, with news, by your life, about the Jews, a blackened one.

He said: 'Desist from a protected town for a Prophet of Makkah from Quraysh, a guided one.'

So I pardoned them with a pardon that does not reproach, and I left them for the punishment of an everlasting day.

And I left them to Allah, hoping for His pardon on the day of reckoning from the blazing Hell.

And I left in it for them from our people a band of men of lineage and praiseworthy courage.

A band in whose wake victory will be, hoping thereby for the reward of the Lord of Muhammad."" [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/533, and he mentioned the rest of the verses.]]

Then when [......] [[An illegible word.]] Tubba' went to their religion, he honored them, and departed from Medina, and took them with him to Yemen. When he approached Yemen to enter it, Himyar prevented him from that and said: "Do not enter it upon us, for you have departed from our religion." He invited them to his religion and said: "It is a religion better than your religion."

They said: "Then judge between us by the fire." In Yemen there was a fire at the foot of a mountain called Nada (so in the manuscript), to which they would bring their disputes; it would judge between them, consuming the wrongdoer and not harming the wronged. When they said this to Tubba', he said: "You have been fair." So his people went out with their idols and what they drew near to in their religion, and the two rabbis went out with their scriptures around their necks, wearing them, until they sat before the fire at the place from which it emerges. The fire came out toward them, but when it approached Himyar, they turned away from it and feared it. Those present from the people called to them and urged them to be patient with it, and they were patient until it overwhelmed them, and it consumed the idols and what they had brought near, and some men of Himyar who carried them. The two rabbis came out with their scriptures around their necks, reciting the Torah, their foreheads sweating, and it did not harm them. The fire recoiled until it returned to its exit from which it had come. At that, Himyar embraced the religion of the two rabbis.

From there came the origin of Judaism in Yemen [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/200.]].

They had a house which they revered, sacrificing beside it and speaking from it while they were upon their polytheism. The two Qurayzah rabbis, whose names were Ka'b and Asad, said to Tubba': "It is nothing but a devil [who deludes them and plays with them], so leave us alone with it." He said: "Then it is your affair with it." They brought out from it a black dog and slaughtered it, then they demolished that house, and its remnants are in Yemen today, as has been mentioned to me.

Abu Dawud narrated from Abu Hatim, from al-Riyashi, who said: Abu Karib As'ad al-Himyari was one of the Tubba's. He believed in the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) seven hundred years before he was sent, and he composed a poem about that:

"I testify concerning Ahmad that he is a messenger from Allah, Creator of souls.

Were my life extended to his lifespan, I would be his in-law and his paternal cousin." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/145.]]

﴿Each one denied the messengers, so My warning was justly due.﴾ That is: the threat of punishment for them, warning the disbelievers of Makkah. Qatadah said: Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, destroyed the people of Tubba', and He did not destroy him. He was one of the kings of Yemen. He marched with armies, conquered lands, and headed for Makkah to demolish the House. It was said to him: "This House has a Lord who protects it." He repented, entered Makkah in the state of ihram, circumambulated the House, and clothed it. He was the first to clothe the House.

﴿Were We then wearied by the first creation?﴾ That is: were We incapable of it, and was the first creation beyond Our power? ﴿Nay, they are in confusion about a new creation﴾, which is the resurrection.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 50, verses 1–15:**

Meccan. It has 1,494 letters, 357 words, and 45 verses.

Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Ahmad al-Mawardi informed us, saying: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sadah al-Karabisi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Muslim ibn Qutaybah narrated to us, from Sa'id, from 'Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surah Qaf, Allah will make the pangs and agonies of death easy for him" [84] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/233.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

**Qaf.** Ibn 'Abbas said: It is one of the names of Allah, the Exalted, by which He swears. Qatadah said: It is one of the names of the Qur'an. Al-Qurazi said: It is the opening of the names of Allah: Qadir (the Able), Qadir (the Capable), Qahir (the Subduer), Qadi (the Judge), and Qabid (the Restrainer). Al-Sha'bi said: It is the opening of the surah. Buraydah, 'Ikrimah, and al-Dahhak said: It is a mountain surrounding the earth, made of green emerald; the greenness of the sky comes from it, the two sides of the sky rest upon it, and what the people have of emerald is what falls from the mountain. This is a narration of Abu al-Hawra', from Ibn 'Abbas.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Dhu al-Qarnayn came to Mount Qaf and saw small mountains around it. He asked it: "What are you?" It said: "I am Qaf." He asked: "What are these mountains around you?" It said: "They are my veins. There is no city among the cities except that it has a vein from it. When Allah wishes to shake that land, He commands me, and I move that vein, and that land is shaken." Dhu al-Qarnayn said: "O Qaf, tell me something of the greatness of Allah." It said: "Indeed, the affair of our Lord is great; attributes fall short of Him, and imaginations come to an end before Him."

He said: "Tell me the least of what can be described of it." It said: "Behind me there is a land, a distance of five hundred years, in a width of five hundred years, of mountains of ice, which crush one another. Were it not for that ice, they would have burned from the heat of Hell."

He said: "Tell me more." It said: "Gabriel, peace be upon him, stands before Allah, the Exalted, and his limbs tremble. Allah creates from each tremor one hundred thousand angels. These angels stand in rows before Allah, the Exalted, with their heads bowed. When Allah permits them to speak, they say: 'There is no god but Allah.' This is His saying: ﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks, none shall speak except one whom the Most Gracious permits, and he speaks what is right﴾ [[Surah al-Naba': 38.]], meaning: there is no god but Allah."

Al-Farra' said: I heard someone say: (Qaf) means: what is to occur has been decreed. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: Its meaning is: stop at Our command and Our prohibition, and do not transgress them. It was also said: Its meaning is: Say, O Muhammad.

Ahmad ibn 'Asim al-Antaki said: It refers to the nearness of Allah, the Exalted, to His servants. Its explanation is His saying: ﴿And We are nearer to him than the jugular vein﴾ [[Surah Qaf: 16.]]. Ibn 'Ata' said: He swears by the strength of the heart of His beloved Muhammad (ﷺ), since he bore the address and it did not affect him, because of the elevation of his state.

**By the Glorious Qur'an.** Noble, honored by Allah, the Great, the All-Aware.

The scholars differed concerning the answer to this oath. The people of Kufa said: the answer is ﴿Nay, but they wonder﴾. Al-Akhfash said: its answer is omitted, and its meaning is: "Qaf. By the Glorious Qur'an, you shall surely be raised." Ibn Kaysan said: its answer is His saying: ﴿...what word he utters...﴾ [the verse]. It was also said: the answer is "We have known."

The answers to oaths are seven: (inna), the emphatic particle, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord is ever watchful﴾ [[Surah al-Fajr: 14.]]; (ma), the negation, as in: ﴿By the morning brightness, your Lord has not forsaken you﴾ [[Surah al-Duha: 1–3.]]; the lam with fatha, as in: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ [[Surah al-Hijr: 92.]]; (in), the light form, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By Allah, we were surely in...﴾ [[Surah al-Shu'ara': 97.]]; (la), as in: ﴿And they swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that Allah will not raise up one who dies﴾ [[Surah al-An'am: 109.]]; (qad), as in: ﴿By the sun and its brightness... he has succeeded who purifies it﴾ [[Surah al-Shams: 1–9.]]; and (bal), as in: ﴿Qaf. By the Glorious Qur'an. Nay, but they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves﴾, whose lineage, lineage, truthfulness, and trustworthiness they knew. ﴿So the disbelievers said: "This is a strange thing"﴾, something astonishing.

﴿When we have died and become dust? That is a far return.﴾ The resurrection is omitted, because the context indicates it. It is said: "I returned him, a return," and he returned, a returning. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if Allah returns you to a faction of them﴾ [[Surah al-Tawbah: 83.]].

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿We have known what the earth consumes of them﴾, meaning what the earth eats of their bones and bodies. It was also said: its meaning is: We have known what decays of them and what remains, because the coccyx is not consumed by the earth, as came in the hadith: "Every son of Adam decays, except the coccyx, from which he was created and from which he will be reassembled" [[85] [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/251 and Musnad Ahmad: 2/499.]]. The bodies of the prophets and martyrs also do not decay.

Al-Suddi said: And death says: We have known who among them will die and who will remain.

﴿And with Us is a Book preserved﴾, protected from the devils and from being effaced or scattered. It is the Preserved Tablet, in which all decreed things are written.

﴿Nay, they denied the truth [the Qur'an] when it came to them, so they are in a confused state.﴾ Abu Hamzah said: Ibn 'Abbas was asked about "marij," and he said: "It is the mixed-up thing. Have you not heard the poet's saying:

"She moved about and sought him within her, so he sprang up as if he were a supple, swaying branch."" [[Taj al-'Arus: 2/100.]]

Al-Walibi reported from him: "a disordered matter." Al-'Awfi reported from him: "a matter of error." Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: "confused." Qatadah said: In this verse, whoever the truth descends upon, his affair becomes confused for him, and his religion becomes obscure to him. Ibn Zayd said: "mixed up." It was also said: "corrupt." It was also said: "changed." All these sayings are close in meaning. The root of "marij" is agitation and restlessness. It is said: "the affair of the people became disordered (maraja)," "the religion became disordered," and "the ring became loose on my finger" (maraja) if it became loose from thinness. The poet said:

"The religion became disordered, so I prepared for it a sturdy, high-withered, well-fleshed (mount)." [[Lisan al-'Arab: 10/408; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/15. "Al-hariq": the withers; "al-kutad": the junction of the two shoulders.]]

In a hadith: "Their covenants and their hopes became disordered (marijat)."

﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We built it and adorned it, and it has no rifts?﴾ That is: cracks and openings; its singular is "fari." Ibn Zayd said: "al-furuj" are things that are scattered and separated from one another. Al-Kisa'i said: There is no disparity or difference in it.

﴿And the earth — We spread it out﴾, extended it over the water. ﴿And We cast in it firm mountains, and caused to grow in it of every beautiful pair, a lovely (plant)﴾, good and noble, by which one is delighted, meaning: gladdened.

﴿As an insight﴾, meaning: We made that an insight. Abu Hatim said: it is in the accusative as an infinitive. ﴿And a reminder for every servant who turns in repentance﴾, meaning: an insight or a reminder of its turning to Him, because whoever is able to create the heavens, the earth, and the plants is able to resurrect them. Among the infinitives similar to "tabsira" are "takmila" and "tafdila," and among the doubled-root nouns are "nakhla" and "ba'ra."

﴿And We sent down from the sky blessed water, and caused to grow by it gardens and grain of the harvest﴾, meaning wheat, barley, and all grains that are harvested, stored, and eaten. He attributed "grain" (habb) to "harvest" (hasid), and they are one thing, because the wording differs, as one says "the mosque of the congregation" and "the spring of the first," and "the sure truth" and "the jugular vein," and the like.

﴿And the tall palm trees﴾. Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, and Qatadah said: tall. 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Had said: its stalk, for its straightness in height. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: upright. ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.﴾ That is, We know him and have power over him. The jugular vein is nearer to him than anything, because his parts and limbs screen one another, but nothing screens God's knowledge from any of this. Al-Wari'd (the jugular vein) is the vein of the neck, which lies between the windpipe (al-halqum) and the two sides of the neck (al-'ilbawain). Its plural is awrad. The word habl (cord) is attached to al-wari'd and then made an attribute of it, since the two words differ. The poet said:

When he does a bad deed, the companion on the right says to the companion on the left: 'Leave it for seven hours; perhaps he will glorify God or seek forgiveness.'"

Al-Hasan said: Indeed the angels avoid a person in two states: when he relieves himself, and when he has intercourse. Abu al-Jawza' and Mujahid said: They record everything against him, even his groaning during his illness. 'Ikrimah said: They record against him only what he will be rewarded for or punished for. Al-Dahhak said: Their seat is under the hair on the chin. The same was narrated by 'Awf from al-Hasan, who said: al-Hasan liked to clean his 'anfaqah (the hair on the lower lip; it was also said to be the hair between the lip and the chin, according to al-Nihayah).

'Ata' and Mujahid said: al-Qa'id is al-Raṣid (the watcher).

Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib informed us in the year three hundred and eighty-six, saying: Abu Muhammad al-Baladhuri narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ayyub al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Tuqa Hisham ibn 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us.

He said: Mubashshir ibn Isma'il al-Halabi narrated to us, from Tammam ibn Najih, from al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayrah and Anas, who both said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "There are no two guardians who raise to God what they have guarded, and God sees at the beginning of the record good and at its end good, but that He says to His angels: 'Bear witness that I have forgiven My servant what lies between the two ends of the record.'"

Abu Sahl ibn Habib informed us, with my reading to him, saying: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Zanjawayh ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Mutarr al-Shaybani narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God has assigned to His believing servant two angels who record his deeds. When he dies, the two angels assigned to him say: 'So-and-so has died, so permit us, and we will ascend to heaven.' God says: 'My heaven is full of My angels who glorify Me.' They say: 'Then we will remain on earth.' God says: 'My earth is full of My creatures who glorify Me.' They say: 'Then where?' He says: 'Stand over the grave of My servant, and magnify Me, glorify Me, and proclaim My oneness, and record that for My servant until the Day of Resurrection.'"

﴿He does not utter a word except that with him is an observer ready.﴾ Yatalaffazu means "speaks." Raqib means "guardian," and 'atid means "present, ready." It has the meaning of ut'tad (ready), from God's saying: ﴿We have prepared (a'tadna)﴾. The Arabs interchange the letter ta' (ت) and the letter dhal (ذ) because their articulation points are close. So they say i'taddtu, a'dhadtu, harada and harata, kabadha and kabata, and similar. The poet said:

*Even if you are absent from me in sight, your remembrance is ready in my heart.*

﴿And the agony of death has come with truth.﴾ That is, the agony of death has come with the truth, but because the agony is the truth, it is attributed to itself because the two names differ. It was also said: al-Haqq (the Truth) is God, Mighty and Majestic, and the figurative sense is: the agony of God's command has come with death. 'Aqil informed us, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us, saying: Juwayr informed us, saying: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Wasil, from Abu Wa'il, who said: When Abu Bakr was dying, 'A'ishah said:

*By your life, wealth does not benefit a man when his breath rattles one day and his chest is constricted.*

Abu Bakr said: "O daughter, it is not that, but it is as God said: ﴿And the agony of death has come with truth. That is what you were trying to avoid.﴾" (From Ibn 'Abbas: tahid means "dislike.") al-Hasan said: "flee." al-Dahhak: "turn away." 'Ata' al-Khurasani: "incline." Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "shrink back."

The root of al-hayd is inclination. It is said: hadtu 'an al-shay' uhayd haydan wa mahidan, meaning I turned away from it. Tarafah said:

*O Abu Mundhir, you desired loyalty and feared it, and you turned away as a camel turns away from the slippery ground.* (al-dahd: pushing.)

﴿And the Horn will be blown. That is the Day of the Threat.﴾ That is the blast of resurrection, the Day God promised to the disbelievers, on which He curses them.

﴿And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness.﴾ The driver drives it to the gathering place, and the witness testifies against it for what it did in the world, good or evil. It was narrated that 'Uthman ibn 'Affan gave a sermon and recited this verse, and said: "The driver drives it to God, and the witness testifies against it for what it did." al-Dahhak said: The driver is the angels, and the witnesses from among themselves are the hands and feet. This is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Abu Hurayrah said: The driver is an angel, and the witness is the deed. The others said: both are of the angels.

God will say to her: ﴿You were in heedlessness of this, so We have removed from you your covering, and your sight today is sharp.﴾ That is, We removed your blindness, lifted your veil, and left you without cover, until you witness it. Your sight today is sharp, strong, penetrating, and firm; you see what was hidden from you.

'Abd al-Wahhab narrated from Mujahid, from his father, about ﴿your sight today is sharp﴾: "Your looking at Me to make clear your balance when your good and bad deeds are weighed."

It was also said that by sight is meant knowledge: knowledge when knowledge no longer benefits him, and sight when sight no longer benefits him.

'Asim al-Jahdari read ﴿You were﴾ with a kasrah on the ta' and on the kaf, returning the writing to the soul.

﴿And his companion will say: This is what is with me, ready.﴾ That is, the angel assigned to him: "this is ready with me, prepared, guarded, and present." Mujahid said: "This is the one who was assigned to me of the children of Adam. I have brought him, and I have brought the register of his deeds." God will say to his companion: ﴿Throw into Hell﴾. al-Khalil and al-Akhfash said: this is the correct speech of the Arabs, to address one person with the dual form. It is good and fine, as one says to a single person: "Woe to you, mount her, drive her, take her, and release her." al-Farra' said: The origin of this is that when a man's helpers come to his camels, sheep, and cattle, two of them come, so the speech about one is spoken as about his two companions. From this is their way of addressing one person in poetry: "my two friends," then he says: "O companion." Imru' al-Qays said:

*My two friends, pass by me over Umm Jundab, and make the heart's sorrows that are tormented be broken.*

And he said:

*Halt, let us weep for the remembrance of a beloved and a dwelling.*

And he said:

*Halt, let us weep for the remembrance of a beloved and 'Urwan.* (The original has this as it is.)

Another said:

*So I said to my two companions, do not hasten us, by pulling out its roots, and cut the shih.* (A plant.)

Abu Thawwan recited:

*If you deter me, O son of 'Affan, I will be deterred; and if you call me, I will defend a protected honor.*

It was also said: it may be that the intent is the repetition of the word, as if he says: "Throw, throw." So alqiya (throw) stands in place of the repetition. It is also possible that alqiya is a true dual, and the address is to both receivers together, or to both the driver and the witness together. al-Hasan read ﴿alqina﴾ with the light emphatic nun, as in God's saying: ﴿and he will surely be imprisoned, and he will surely be among the humiliated.﴾

﴿Every obstinate disbeliever, who prevents good, transgressor, doubter, who set up with God another god, so throw him into the severe punishment.﴾ ʿAnid means disobedient, turning away from the truth. Mujahid and 'Ikrimah said: he is opposed to the truth and defiant against God.

Mannā' lil-khayr (preventing the good): that is, from the obligatory zakat and every due right in his wealth.

Mu'tad (transgressor): unjust. Murib (doubter): skeptical. Qatadah said: "doubting."

The meaning is that he is within the doubt. ﴿Who set up with God another god.﴾ It was also said: this was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. By his saying ﴿preventing the good﴾ he meant that he used to prevent his nephews from Islam, saying: "If any of you enters the religion of Muhammad, I will not benefit him with anything as long as I live."

﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.﴾ That is, We know him and have power over him. The jugular vein is nearer to him than anything, because his parts and limbs screen one another, but nothing screens God's knowledge from any of this. Al-Wari'd (the jugular vein) is the vein of the neck, which lies between the windpipe (al-halqum) and the two sides of the neck (al-'ilbawain). Its plural is awrad. The word habl (cord) is attached to al-wari'd and then made an attribute of it, since the two words differ. The poet said:

*She became cold toward the wicked, so he came running, when he was stirred and his vein swelled.*

﴿When the two receivers receive, one seated on the right and one on the left.﴾ That is, the two angels assigned to you receive and record. God assigned to every person, though He knows his circumstances, two angels by night and two by day, who guard his deeds and record their traces, as a confirmation of the proof against him. One is on his right and records the good deeds, and the other on his left and records the bad deeds. This is God's saying: ﴿one seated on the right and one on the left.﴾ He did not say "two seated." The people of Basra said: He meant "a seated one on the right and a seated one on the left," and he suffices with one of them for the other, as in the poet's saying:

*We are content with what we have, and you with what you have, though our opinions differ.*

And in the saying of al-Farazdaq:

*I have guaranteed for whoever came to me what he committed, and he refused, and I was not treacherous.*

He did not say "treacherous" in the dual. The word qa'id (seated) and qa'id (one who sits) are like samee' (hearing), 'aleem (knowing), and qadeer (powerful). The people of Kufa said: He meant "seated" as a collective, so he returned it to the category and put the singular in place of the plural, as with rasool (messenger), which is used for two, and for more than two. God said of two: ﴿Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds﴾. The poet said:

*Convey my message to her, and the best messenger is the one most knowledgeable about the aspects of the news.*

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Salim al-Khatili narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ayyub al-Rakhani narrated to us, saying: Jamil ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Artat ibn al-Ash'ath al-'Adawi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the seat of your two angels is on your two front teeth, your tongue is their pen, your saliva is their ink, and you are running, I think he said, in what does not concern you. Be ashamed before God and before them."

And al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Manjawayh al-Dinawari informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn al-'Abbas ibn Mihran narrated to us, saying: Talut narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 50, verse 27–35:

Her companion (qarin) said: that is, the devil who was assigned to this stubborn disbeliever. ﴿Our Lord, I did not make him rebel; I did not mislead him, and I did not lead him astray.﴾

Al-Qurazi said: "I did not compel him to rebellion." ﴿But he was in far-off error﴾ from the truth. Thus his devil disowns him.

Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil said: "Her companion" means the angel. This is because al-Walid ibn al-Mughira would say to the angel who used to record the bad deeds: "My Lord, he hastened me." The angel would reply: ﴿Our Lord, I did not make him rebel; I did not make him hasten.﴾

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the disbeliever says, "My Lord, the angel added to what he wrote against me." The angel says: ﴿Our Lord, I did not make him rebel,﴾ meaning: I did not add to what he did, and I wrote nothing except what he said and did.

Then Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿Do not dispute before Me; I had already sent forward to you the warning.﴾ Meaning: I have already decreed what I decree. ﴿I had already sent forward to you the threat in the Qur'an,﴾ I warned you and gave you notice, ﴿so there is no changing My word or My threat.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: They offered excuses without any valid excuse, so Allah nullified their argument and refuted their claim with the statement ﴿The word is not changed before Me,﴾ which is His saying: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together.﴾ [Surah Hud: 119.]

Al-Farra' said: its meaning is that it is not falsified before Me, because of My knowledge of the unseen. ﴿And I am not unjust to the servants,﴾ so that I punish them without crime or repay good with evil.

﴿On the Day We say to Hell, "Are you filled?"﴾ Qatadah, al-A'raj, Shaybah, and Nafi' read (taqulu) with the "ta" (tā'), and Abu Bakr narrated the same from 'Asim, following the sense of His saying: "Do not dispute before Me." Al-Hasan read yawma yuqalu, and the rest read yawma naqulu with the "nun" (nūn). ﴿To Hell, "Are you filled?"﴾ because of what preceded of His promise to fill it: that He will fill it ﴿with jinn and men all together.﴾ This question from Him is in the manner of affirming His report, confirming His promise, rebuking the people of His punishment, and alerting all His servants.

﴿And it says, "Is there any more?"﴾ It may be a denial, meaning "there is no more," and it may be an interrogation, meaning "Is there any more?" so He adds more. "Hal" (هل) is suitable for both meanings together, because interrogation contains a kind of denial and a trace of negation.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah, glorified and exalted, had already decreed His word: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together." When the people were gathered and the enemies of Allah were driven to the Fire in groups, they began to be thrust into Hell, group after group. Nothing was cast into Hell without vanishing in it, and nothing could fill it.

Then it says: "Have I not been made to fill?" He placed His foot upon it, then says to it, "Are you filled?" It says: "Qat, qat (enough, enough), I am filled, there is no more."

Ibn 'Abbas said: Nothing filled it until the foot of Allah touched it, and then it contracted, so there was no place left for a needle.

The evidence for this interpretation is what

'Aqil informed us, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us, saying: Ibn Jarir informed us, saying: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Hell will not cease to have people cast into it, and it will say, 'Is there any more?' until the Lord of the worlds places His foot in it, and parts of it draw toward one another, and it says, 'Enough, enough, by Your might and Your generosity.' And there will still be surplus in Paradise until Allah, glorified is He, creates a new creation for it, and they will dwell in the surplus of Paradise." [91] [Sahih al-Bukhari: 8/167; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/220, with variations.]

And Ibn Hamdun informed us, saying: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr, and Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayra narrated to us, from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Paradise and the Fire disputed. The Fire said: 'I have been given the arrogant and the tyrants.' Paradise said: 'What is wrong with me that only the weak among people and their refuse enter me?' Allah, glorified is He, said to Paradise: 'You are only My mercy; I show mercy through you to whom I will of My servants.' And He said to the Fire: 'You are only My punishment; I punish through you whom I will of My servants. Each of you has its fullness. As for the Fire, they will be cast into it, and it will say, "Is there any more?" and it will not be filled until Allah, glorified and exalted, places His foot in it, and it says, "Qat, qat," then it is filled, and parts of it draw toward one another, and Allah does not wrong any of His creation. As for Paradise, Allah, mighty and majestic, creates a new creation for it.'" [92] [Sahih al-Bukhari: 6/48; Sahih Muslim: 8/151, with slight variation.]

I say: These two hadiths concerning the mention of the "foot" (qadam) and the "leg" (rijl) are sound and well known, and they have chains from the hadith of Abu Hurayra and Anas. I have omitted mentioning them out of dislike of lengthiness. The meaning of the "qadam" mentioned in this transmitted report is a people whom Allah sends forward to Hell, filling it with them, who were already decreed in His knowledge to be heading there and abiding in it. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: I asked al-Khalil ibn Ahmad about the meaning of this hadith, and he said: "They are a people whom Allah has sent forward to the Fire." 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mubarak said: "They are those whom it was already decreed in His knowledge are of the people of the Fire."

Everything that is sent forward is called "qadam." Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿that they have a sure standing (qadam sidq) with their Lord,﴾ meaning good deeds they sent forward. A poet, blaming a man, said:

"Qa'adat bihi qadam al-fujjar wa ghuditra... wa 'awwadu rabbin asbabuhu min fitnatin min khaliq"

meaning: he has nothing to boast of with them.

Al-Awza'i, however, narrated this hadith from Hassan ibn 'Atiyya, "until the Jabbar places His foot" with the qaf kasra. Wahb ibn Munabbih also narrated it likewise, and said: Allah, glorified is He, had created a people before Adam called "al-Qadam," whose heads were like the heads of dogs and flies, and the rest of their bodies like the bodies of the children of Adam. They disobeyed their Lord, and Allah destroyed them, and Allah will fill Hell with them when it asks for more. As for "rijl," it means a large number of people and others.

﴿And it says, "Is there any more?"﴾ It may be a denial, meaning "there is no more," and it may be an interrogation, meaning "Is there any more?" so He adds more. "Hal" (هل) is suitable for both meanings together, because interrogation contains a kind of denial and a trace of negation.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah, glorified and exalted, had already decreed His word: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together." When the people were gathered and the enemies of Allah were driven to the Fire in groups, they began to be thrust into Hell, group after group. Nothing was cast into Hell without vanishing in it, and nothing could fill it.

Then it says: "Have I not been made to fill?" He placed His foot upon it, then says to it, "Are you filled?" It says: "Qat, qat (enough, enough), I am filled, there is no more."

Ibn 'Abbas said: Nothing filled it until the foot of Allah touched it, and then it contracted, so there was no place left for a needle.

The evidence for this interpretation is what

'Aqil informed us, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us, saying: Ibn Jarir informed us, saying: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Hell will not cease to have people cast into it, and it will say, 'Is there any more?' until the Lord of the worlds places His foot in it, and parts of it draw toward one another, and it says, 'Enough, enough, by Your might and Your generosity.' And there will still be surplus in Paradise until Allah, glorified is He, creates a new creation for it, and they will dwell in the surplus of Paradise." [91] [Sahih al-Bukhari: 8/167; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/220, with variations.]

And Ibn Hamdun informed us, saying: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr, and Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayra narrated to us, from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Paradise and the Fire disputed. The Fire said: 'I have been given the arrogant and the tyrants.' Paradise said: 'What is wrong with me that only the weak among people and their refuse enter me?' Allah, glorified is He, said to Paradise: 'You are only My mercy; I show mercy through you to whom I will of My servants.' And He said to the Fire: 'You are only My punishment; I punish through you whom I will of My servants. Each of you has its fullness. As for the Fire, they will be cast into it, and it will say, "Is there any more?" and it will not be filled until Allah, glorified and exalted, places His foot in it, and it says, "Qat, qat," then it is filled, and parts of it draw toward one another, and Allah does not wrong any of His creation. As for Paradise, Allah, mighty and majestic, creates a new creation for it.'" [92] [Sahih al-Bukhari: 6/48; Sahih Muslim: 8/151, with slight variation.]

I say: These two hadiths concerning the mention of the "foot" (qadam) and the "leg" (rijl) are sound and well known, and they have chains from the hadith of Abu Hurayra and Anas. I have omitted mentioning them out of dislike of lengthiness. The meaning of the "qadam" mentioned in this transmitted report is a people whom Allah sends forward to Hell, filling it with them, who were already decreed in His knowledge to be heading there and abiding in it. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: I asked al-Khalil ibn Ahmad about the meaning of this hadith, and he said: "They are a people whom Allah has sent forward to the Fire." 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mubarak said: "They are those whom it was already decreed in His knowledge are of the people of the Fire."

Everything that is sent forward is called "qadam." Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿that they have a sure standing (qadam sidq) with their Lord,﴾ meaning good deeds they sent forward. A poet, blaming a man, said:

"Qa'adat bihi qadam al-fujjar wa ghuditra... wa 'awwadu rabbin asbabuhu min fitnatin min khaliq"

meaning: he has nothing to boast of with them.

Al-Awza'i, however, narrated this hadith from Hassan ibn 'Atiyya, "until the Jabbar places His foot" with the qaf kasra. Wahb ibn Munabbih also narrated it likewise, and said: Allah, glorified is He, had created a people before Adam called "al-Qadam," whose heads were like the heads of dogs and flies, and the rest of their bodies like the bodies of the children of Adam. They disobeyed their Lord, and Allah destroyed them, and Allah will fill Hell with them when it asks for more. As for "rijl," it means a large number of people and others.

It is said: "I saw a man (rajul) from among the people," and "a man (rajul) of the good horses passed by us." Al-Asma'i said: I heard some Bedouins say: "No prophet was destroyed over a man as Moses was destroyed over a man," meaning the Copts. A poet said:

"Fa-marra bina rajulun min al-nas wa-nzawa... ilayhim min al-hayyi al-yamaniyyina arjulu
Qaba'ila min Lakhmin wa Himyara... 'ala ibnay Nizarin bil-'adawati uhfulu"

[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/19.]

This interpretation is confirmed by the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying within the hadith: "and Allah does not wrong any of His creation," which indicates that what is cast into the Fire is a part of His creation. Some of them said: he meant the "qadam" of some of His angels, and attributed it to Him, as in His saying: ﴿and ask the town﴾. And Allah knows best.

﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the God-fearing﴾, made near and brought close, ﴿not far off﴾ from them, so that they see it before they enter it. This is emphasis. It will be said to them: "This is what you were promised in the world through the tongues of the prophets."

﴿For every oft-returning (awwab)﴾: one who repents often, according to al-Dahhak. It was also said: one who returns to obedience, according to Ibn Zayd. Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ata' said: the awwab is one who glorifies (musabbih), from His saying: ﴿O mountains, echo with him (awwibi) [in glorification].﴾ al-Hakam ibn 'Uyayna said: he is one who remembers Allah in solitude. al-Sha'bi and Mujahid said: one who recalls his sins in solitude and then seeks forgiveness for them. Qatadah: the one who prays. Muqatil ibn Hayyan: the obedient. 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr: one who does not rise from his sitting until he has asked Allah's forgiveness. Abu Bakr al-Warraq: one who relies upon Allah, glorified is He, in ease and hardship, and does not turn to anyone other than Allah. al-Mahasini: one who turns his heart back to his Lord. al-Qasim: one who is occupied with nothing but Allah.

﴿Guardian (hafiz)﴾: Ibn 'Abbas said: one who guards his sins until he turns away from them. Qatadah: one who guards what Allah has entrusted to him of His right and His blessing. Also from Ibn 'Abbas: one who guards the command of Allah. al-Dahhak: one who guards himself and takes care of it. 'Ata': one who remembers Allah in a desolate land. al-Sha'bi: one who watches over himself. Abu Bakr al-Warraq: one who guards his times, his concerns, and his steps. Sahl: one who guards the acts of obedience and the commands.

﴿Who feared the Most Merciful unseen﴾ (man khashiya): there are two grammatical possibilities: the genitive (khafd) as a qualifier of "awwab," and the nominative (raf') as a new sentence, whose predicate is in His saying "enter it." The meaning of the verse: one who feared the Most Merciful in the unseen and did not see Him. al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: meaning in solitude, where no one is present. al-Hasan said: when he lowers the curtain and closes the door.

﴿And comes with a heart turned penitently (munib)﴾: turning in submission to Allah's obedience. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: the sign of the munib is that he knows the sanctity of Allah, is loyal to Him, humble before His lawful things, and abandons the desires of his own soul.

﴿Enter it﴾: that is, it will be said to people of this description: ﴿Enter it in peace﴾, in safety from punishment, and the peace of Allah and His angels be upon them. It was also said: safety from the loss of blessing and the descent of retribution.

﴿That is the Day of Eternity for them; they will have whatever they wish therein, and with Us is more﴾: meaning the increase for them in blessings beyond what had occurred to their minds. Jabir and Anas said: it is gazing upon the Face of Allah, glorified and exalted, without asking how.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 50, verse 36–45:

﴿وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ هُمْ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُمْ بَطْشاً فَنَقَّبُوا فِي الْبِلادِ﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: "athirū" (they searched/traversed).

Mujahid said: "ḍarabū" (they travelled). al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "ṭāfū" (they went around). al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said: "dawḥū" (they wandered). al-Farrāʾ said: "kharaqū" (they pierced through). al-Mu'arrikh said: "tabāʿadū" (they went far away). From this is the verse of Imru' al-Qays:

"Indeed I have searched through the horizons until / I was content with the spoil of returning."

[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/226.]]

al-Ḥasan recited "fa-naqabū" with a light qaf (fa-naqabū). al-Sulamī and Yaḥyā ibn Maʿmar recited it with a doubled qaf (naqqabū), as a threat and warning, meaning: travel through the lands, move across the earth, and see whether there is any escape (maḥīṣ) from death and God's command, glorified is He.

﴿إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ﴾ — that is, in the towns that were destroyed and the lessons that were mentioned — ﴿لَذِكْرى﴾ is a reminder ﴿لِمَنْ كانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ﴾, that is, intellect. The intellect is referred to by "heart" because it is its place and its follower. Qatadah said: ﴿لِمَنْ كانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ﴾ means a living heart, similar to ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ مَنْ كانَ حَيًّا﴾. al-Shiblī said: a heart present with God, never heedless of Him for the blink of an eye. Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh said: the heart is of two kinds: a heart stuffed with the concerns of this world, so that when a matter of the Hereafter arrives it does not know what to do because of its preoccupation with the world; and a heart stuffed with the terrors of the Hereafter, so that when a matter of this world arrives it does not know what to do because its heart is absorbed in the Hereafter. I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Ḥabībī say: I asked Abu al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-ʿAbbād about this verse, and he said: its meaning is ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَذِكْرى لِمَنْ كانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ﴾ — a heart that is steadfast and does not turn away from God in ease or hardship.

﴿أَوْ أَلْقَى السَّمْعَ﴾ — that is, listens to the Qur'an. The Arabs say: "alqi ilayya samʿaka," meaning listen. al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: it means the face of the listener, and it is turned toward the remembrance, as one says "ittabiʿī ilayhi."

﴿وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ﴾ — that is, present of heart. Qatadah said: he is a witness to what is recited and heard in the Book of God, glorified is He, of the love of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his mention.

﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَما بَيْنَهُما فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ وَما مَسَّنا مِنْ لُغُوبٍ﴾ — fatigue and weariness.

It was revealed concerning the Jews, when they said: "O Muhammad, tell us what God created of creation in these six days?"

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "God Most High created the earth on Sunday and Monday, the mountains on Tuesday, and the cities, rivers and sustenance on Wednesday, and the heavens and the angels on Thursday, until three hours of Friday; and in the first of the three hours He created the appointed terms, in the second the calamity, and in the third Adam."

He said: They said: "You have spoken the truth, if you complete it." He said: "And what is that?" They said: "Then He rested on Saturday and reclined upon the Throne." So God Most High revealed this verse. [93] [[Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 6/124; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari 26/229, with slight variation.]]

﴿فَاصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ﴾ — for God is watchful over them. ﴿وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ﴾ — that is, say: "Glory be to God and praise be to God." This is from ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī. Others said: pray by the command and enabling of your Lord. ﴿قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ﴾ — that is, the dawn prayer; ﴿وَقَبْلَ الْغُرُوبِ﴾ — the afternoon prayer. It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that ﴿وَقَبْلَ الْغُرُوبِ﴾ means the noon and afternoon prayers. ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ﴾ — that is, the two evening prayers (the evening and night prayers). Mujahid said: "from the night entirely," that is, the night prayer, whenever one prays it.

﴿وَأَدْبارَ السُّجُودِ﴾ — ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, ʿAlī ibn Abi Ṭalib, Abu Hurayra, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, al-Nakhaʿī, al-Shaʿbī and al-Awzāʿī said: "adbār al-sujūd" refers to the two rakʿahs after Maghrib, and "idbār al-nujūm" to the two rakʿahs before Fajr. This is the narration of al-ʿAwfī from Ibn ʿAbbas. It has also been transmitted from him as a marfūʿ report:

Aqil informed us, saying: al-Muʿāfā informed us, saying: Ibn Jarir told us, saying: Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Fudayl told us, from Rashid ibn Kurayb, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: "O Ibn ʿAbbas, two rakʿahs after Maghrib are adbār al-sujūd."

Anas ibn Malik said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever prays two rakʿahs after Maghrib before speaking, his prayer is recorded in ʿIlliyyīn."

[[al-Muntazaʿ al-Mukhtar: 1/225; Iʿanat al-Talibin: 1/285.]] Anas said: he recites in the first rakʿah "Qul yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn," and in the second "Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad."

Muqatil said: their time lasts as long as the twilight has not disappeared. Mujahid said: it is glorifying with the tongue after the obligatory prayers, and he narrated it from Ibn ʿAbbas. Ibn Zayd said: it is the voluntary prayers after the obligatory ones.

The reciters differed regarding His saying "wa-adbār." al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj, Kharija, Abu ʿAmr, Yaʿqub, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī read it with an open alif (wa-adbāra), and this was preferred by Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Ḥātim.

The others read it with a kasra (wa-idbāra), and this is the reading of ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbas.

Some scholars said regarding His saying ﴿قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ﴾: it refers to the two rakʿahs of Fajr; and ﴿وَقَبْلَ الْغُرُوبِ﴾: the two rakʿahs before Maghrib.

ʿUmārah ibn Zādhān narrated from Thumāmah ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: "The people of understanding among the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) used to pray the two rakʿahs before Maghrib."

Shuʿbah narrated from Yazid ibn Jubayr, from Khalid ibn Maʿdan, from Raghbān, mawla of Ḥabīb ibn Maslama, who said: "I saw the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) rushing to them as they rush to the obligatory prayer," meaning the two rakʿahs before Maghrib.

Qatadah said: "I did not meet anyone who prayed the two rakʿahs before Maghrib except Anas and Abu Barzah."

﴿وَاسْتَمِعْ﴾ — O Muhammad, listen for the Cry of the Resurrection. ﴿يَوْمَ يُنادِ الْمُنادِ﴾ — Israfil, peace be upon him, will call; the decayed bones, the severed joints, the torn flesh and the scattered hair will come to him: "Indeed God [commands you] to gather yourselves for the judgment." ﴿مِنْ مَكانٍ قَرِيبٍ﴾ — the rock of Jerusalem, which is the center of the earth and the nearest part of the earth to the heavens by eighteen miles. ﴿يَوْمَ يَسْمَعُونَ الصَّيْحَةَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ — this is the final blast. ﴿ذلِكَ يَوْمُ الْخُرُوجِ﴾ — the day of coming forth from the graves. ﴿إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي وَنُمِيتُ وَإِلَيْنَا الْمَصِيرُ﴾. ﴿يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ الْأَرْضُ عَنْهُمْ سِراعاً﴾ — plural of "sarīʿ" (swift), in the accusative as a circumstantial clause; its sense is: they will come forth hastening. ﴿ذلِكَ حَشْرٌ عَلَيْنا يَسِيرٌ﴾. ﴿نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِما يَقُولُونَ وَما أَنْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِجَبَّارٍ﴾ — one who imposes control, a subduer who compels them to Islam; I was only sent as a reminder and a renewer.

Tha'lab said: forms of the pattern "fa''āl" have come with the meaning of "maf'il," and these are irregular: "jabbār" meaning "mujbir" (compeller), "darrāk" meaning "mudrik" (overtaker), "sarrāʿ" meaning "musriʿ" (hastener), "bakkāʾ" meaning "mubkī" (one who makes weep), "ʿaddāʾ" meaning "muʿdī" (one who makes run). It has also been read: ﴿وَما أَهْدِيكُمْ إِلَّا سَبِيلَ الرَّشادِ﴾ [[Surah Ghafir: 29.]] with the meaning "al-murshid" (the guide). I heard Abu Mansur al-Jamshadhi say: I heard Abu Hamid al-Jazarnaji say: "al-ʿawn" is a sword that cuts down, meaning "musqit" (one who causes to fall).

Some said: "al-jabbār" derives from their saying "jabartuhu ʿalā al-amr," meaning "ajbartuhu" (I compelled him to the matter), and this is the dialect of Kinana; both are two dialects.

al-Farrāʾ said: "al-jabbār" was placed in the position of the sultan from "al-jabriyya" (coercion). He said: al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:

"And the day of sorrow when Maʿadd gathered, / and the people were all but us in religion,
The resolve of the compeller disobeyed us until / we attacked al-Jawf at dawn, a thousand of our marked men."

[[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 5/2118.]] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/237.]] He said: he meant by "al-jabbār" al-Mundhir ibn al-Nuʿman, on account of his rule.

﴿فَذَكِّرْ﴾ — O Muhammad, ﴿بِالْقُرْآنِ مَنْ يَخافُ وَعِيدِ﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: they said, "O Messenger of God, if only you would warn us?" And so it was revealed: ﴿فَذَكِّرْ بِالْقُرْآنِ مَنْ يَخافُ وَعِيدِ﴾.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 50, verse 36–45:

﴿وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ هُمْ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُمْ بَطْشاً فَنَقَّبُوا فِي الْبِلادِ﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: "athirū" (they searched/traversed).

Mujahid said: "ḍarabū" (they travelled). al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "ṭāfū" (they went around). al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said: "dawḥū" (they wandered). al-Farrāʾ said: "kharaqū" (they pierced through). al-Mu'arrikh said: "tabāʿadū" (they went far away). From this is the verse of Imru' al-Qays:

"Indeed I have searched through the horizons until / I was content with the spoil of returning."

[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/226.]]

The intellect is referred to by "heart" because it is its place and its follower. Qatadah said: ﴿لِمَنْ كانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ﴾ means a living heart, similar to ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ مَنْ كانَ حَيًّا﴾. al-Shiblī said: a heart present with God, never heedless of Him for the blink of an eye. I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Ḥabībī say: I asked Abu al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-ʿAbbād about this verse, and he said: its meaning is ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَذِكْرى لِمَنْ كانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ﴾ — a heart that is steadfast and does not turn away from God in ease or hardship.

﴿أَوْ أَلْقَى السَّمْعَ﴾ — that is, listens to the Qur'an. The Arabs say: "alqi ilayya samʿaka," meaning listen. al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: it means the face of the listener, and it is turned toward the remembrance, as one says "ittabiʿī ilayhi."

﴿وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ﴾ — that is, present of heart. Qatadah said: he is a witness to what is recited and heard in the Book of God, glorified is He, of the love of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his mention.

﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَما بَيْنَهُما فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ وَما مَسَّنا مِنْ لُغُوبٍ﴾ — fatigue and weariness.

It was revealed concerning the Jews, when they said: "O Muhammad, tell us what God created of creation in these six days?"

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "God Most High created the earth on Sunday and Monday, the mountains on Tuesday, and the cities, rivers and sustenance on Wednesday, and the heavens and the angels on Thursday, until three hours of Friday; and in the first of the three hours He created the appointed terms, in the second the calamity, and in the third Adam."

He said: They said: "You have spoken the truth, if you complete it." He said: "And what is that?" They said: "Then He rested on Saturday and reclined upon the Throne." So God Most High revealed this verse. [93] [[Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 6/124; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari 26/229, with slight variation.]]

﴿فَاصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ﴾ — for God is watchful over them. ﴿وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ﴾ — that is, say: "Glory be to God and praise be to God." This is from ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī.
