He said: They said: "You have spoken the truth, if you complete it." He said: "And what is that?" They said: "Then He rested on Saturday and reclined upon the Throne." So God Most High revealed this verse. [93] [[Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 6/124; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari 26/229, with slight variation.]]

﴿فَاصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ﴾ — for God is watchful over them. ﴿وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ﴾ — that is, say: "Glory be to God and praise be to God." This is from ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī. Others said: pray by the command and enabling of your Lord. ﴿قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ﴾ — that is, the dawn prayer; ﴿وَقَبْلَ الْغُرُوبِ﴾ — the afternoon prayer. It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that ﴿وَقَبْلَ الْغُرُوبِ﴾ means the noon and afternoon prayers. ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ﴾ — that is, the two evening prayers (the evening and night prayers). Mujahid said: "from the night entirely," that is, the night prayer, whenever one prays it.

﴿وَأَدْبارَ السُّجُودِ﴾ — ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, ʿAlī ibn Abi Ṭalib, Abu Hurayra, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, al-Nakhaʿī, al-Shaʿbī and al-Awzāʿī said: "adbār al-sujūd" refers to the two rakʿahs after Maghrib, and "idbār al-nujūm" to the two rakʿahs before Fajr. This is the narration of al-ʿAwfī from Ibn ʿAbbas. It has also been transmitted from him as a marfūʿ report:

Aqil informed us, saying: al-Muʿāfā informed us, saying: Ibn Jarir told us, saying: Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Fudayl told us, from Rashid ibn Kurayb, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: "O Ibn ʿAbbas, two rakʿahs after Maghrib are adbār al-sujūd."

Anas ibn Malik said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever prays two rakʿahs after Maghrib before speaking, his prayer is recorded in ʿIlliyyīn."

[[al-Muntazaʿ al-Mukhtar: 1/225; Iʿanat al-Talibin: 1/285.]] Anas said: he recites in the first rakʿah "Qul yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn," and in the second "Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad."

Muqatil said: their time lasts as long as the twilight has not disappeared. Mujahid said: it is glorifying with the tongue after the obligatory prayers, and he narrated it from Ibn ʿAbbas. Ibn Zayd said: it is the voluntary prayers after the obligatory ones.

The reciters differed regarding His saying "wa-adbār." al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj, Kharija, Abu ʿAmr, Yaʿqub, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī read it with an open alif (wa-adbāra), and this was preferred by Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Ḥātim.

The others read it with a kasra (wa-idbāra), and this is the reading of ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbas.

Some scholars said regarding His saying ﴿قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ﴾: it refers to the two rakʿahs of Fajr; and ﴿وَقَبْلَ الْغُرُوبِ﴾: the two rakʿahs before Maghrib.

ʿUmārah ibn Zādhān narrated from Thumāmah ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: "The people of understanding among the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) used to pray the two rakʿahs before Maghrib."

Shuʿbah narrated from Yazid ibn Jubayr, from Khalid ibn Maʿdan, from Raghbān, mawla of Ḥabīb ibn Maslama, who said: "I saw the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) rushing to them as they rush to the obligatory prayer," meaning the two rakʿahs before Maghrib.

Qatadah said: "I did not meet anyone who prayed the two rakʿahs before Maghrib except Anas and Abu Barzah."

﴿وَاسْتَمِعْ﴾ — O Muhammad, listen for the Cry of the Resurrection. ﴿يَوْمَ يُنادِ الْمُنادِ﴾ — Israfil, peace be upon him, will call; the decayed bones, the severed joints, the torn flesh and the scattered hair will come to him: "Indeed God [commands you] to gather yourselves for the judgment." ﴿مِنْ مَكانٍ قَرِيبٍ﴾ — the rock of Jerusalem, which is the center of the earth and the nearest part of the earth to the heavens by eighteen miles. ﴿يَوْمَ يَسْمَعُونَ الصَّيْحَةَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ — this is the final blast. ﴿ذلِكَ يَوْمُ الْخُرُوجِ﴾ — the day of coming forth from the graves. ﴿إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي وَنُمِيتُ وَإِلَيْنَا الْمَصِيرُ﴾. ﴿يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ الْأَرْضُ عَنْهُمْ سِراعاً﴾ — plural of "sarīʿ" (swift), in the accusative as a circumstantial clause; its sense is: they will come forth hastening. ﴿ذلِكَ حَشْرٌ عَلَيْنا يَسِيرٌ﴾. ﴿نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِما يَقُولُونَ وَما أَنْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِجَبَّارٍ﴾ — one who imposes control, a subduer who compels them to Islam; I was only sent as a reminder and a renewer.

Tha'lab said: forms of the pattern "fa''āl" have come with the meaning of "maf'il," and these are irregular: "jabbār" meaning "mujbir" (compeller), "darrāk" meaning "mudrik" (overtaker), "sarrāʿ" meaning "musriʿ" (hastener), "bakkāʾ" meaning "mubkī" (one who makes weep), "ʿaddāʾ" meaning "muʿdī" (one who makes run). It has also been read: ﴿وَما أَهْدِيكُمْ إِلَّا سَبِيلَ الرَّشادِ﴾ [[Surah Ghafir: 29.]] with the meaning "al-murshid" (the guide). I heard Abu Mansur al-Jamshadhi say: I heard Abu Hamid al-Jazarnaji say: "al-ʿawn" is a sword that cuts down, meaning "musqit" (one who causes to fall).

Some said: "al-jabbār" derives from their saying "jabartuhu ʿalā al-amr," meaning "ajbartuhu" (I compelled him to the matter), and this is the dialect of Kinana; both are two dialects.

al-Farrāʾ said: "al-jabbār" was placed in the position of the sultan from "al-jabriyya" (coercion). He said: al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:

"And the day of sorrow when Maʿadd gathered, / and the people were all but us in religion,
The resolve of the compeller disobeyed us until / we attacked al-Jawf at dawn, a thousand of our marked men."

[[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 5/2118.]] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/237.]] He said: he meant by "al-jabbār" al-Mundhir ibn al-Nuʿman, on account of his rule.

﴿فَذَكِّرْ﴾ — O Muhammad, ﴿بِالْقُرْآنِ مَنْ يَخافُ وَعِيدِ﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: they said, "O Messenger of God, if only you would warn us?" And so it was revealed: ﴿فَذَكِّرْ بِالْقُرْآنِ مَنْ يَخافُ وَعِيدِ﴾.
